description:
Hey,

we are Layan & Mia, participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Tel Aviv! 

Our team, ML Mappers, is tackling the exciting challenge of "Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars". 

Our goal is to map and analyze terrestrial environments on Earth  that share characteristics with the Moon or Mars. We want to find the best analogs to help future space missions 

We are excited to tackle this challenge together as a team!
summary:
AnaloGraph is a decision-support tool that finds the best places on Earth to rehearse a specific Mars mission at a specific Mars site. The challenge notes that no Earth location perfectly reproduces another planet, and that different places are useful analogs for different characteristics. We turned that into our method: instead of one "most Mars-like" ranking, AnaloGraph scores Earth places separately for four mission profiles (ice drilling, landing and rover driving, habitat and crew, life detection) against six real Mars sites, including the Jezero, Gale, Meridiani and InSight landing sites.

We measure nine terrain, temperature and environment features the same way on both planets from open NASA and ESA data (Copernicus DEM, MOLA, MODIS, the Mars Climate Database, SWIM). Mission rules filter places first, a match score ranks them, and a Gap Index states what Earth still can't simulate. In a blind test, AnaloGraph ranked known Mars analogs above clearly non-Mars-like places (AUC 0.89, against 0.74 for equal weights). A regional scan of 444 squares found 22 new candidates. The Negev ranks first for rover practice near Jezero. This helps mission planners choose test sites faster, more honestly, and beyond the usual shortlist.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

AnaloGraph finds the best places on Earth to rehearse a specific Mars mission at a specific Mars site. Instead of one "most Mars-like" list, it produces a mission brief for each combination: three recommended Earth places, why they match, which famous analogs fail, and what Earth cannot simulate.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Same measurements on both planets: nine features (mean slope, steep-slope share, roughness, relief, day-night temperature swing, coldest night, dryness, bare ground, ground ice), from open data and resampled to the same 463 m resolution.

2. Four mission profiles (ice drilling, landing and rover driving, habitat and crew, life detection), each with its own Mars target sites, weights and pass/fail rules, like NASA's landing-site slope limits.

3. A match score (0-100) that ranks Earth places for one mission and one Mars site, using only the features that matter for it.

4. A Gap Index that measures how far even the best match still is from Mars, plus gaps no Earth site can close: magnetic field, radiation, air pressure and gravity.

5. Confidence: every ranking is re-scored 500 times with shifted weights.

We scored 23 Earth places against 6 Mars sites, then scanned 444 squares of 20 km across the Negev, Sinai, southern Jordan and nearby areas.

RESULTS AND VALIDATION

In a blind test, AnaloGraph ranked 11 known Mars analogs above 5 clearly non-Mars-like controls (AUC 0.89, against 0.74 when every feature counts equally). Atacama ranked first for life detection at every Mars site. Timna Valley, HaMakhtesh HaGadol and Makhtesh Ramon beat every famous analog for rover practice near Jezero. The regional scan found 22 places not on any list that beat our best site.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Mission teams can choose test sites faster, compare options transparently, and see openly what a field test will not cover. Finding new, accessible analogs close to home can make analog research cheaper and open it to more countries and students.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, rasterio, PyYAML, folium), Google Earth Engine, HTML/CSS, GitHub and GitHub Pages. Data: ESA Copernicus DEM GLO-30, NASA MOLA, NASA MODIS land surface temperature, TerraClimate, ESA WorldCover, the Mars Climate Database and NASA SWIM ice maps.

CREATIVITY

We answered the challenge's own statement, that different places are analogs for different characteristics, by making analog quality depend on the mission and the site. Two other ideas we haven't seen in analog lists: an honest Gap Index, and a planned biological measure. Magnetotactic bacteria would align 92% on Earth but only 16% at the InSight site, which turns the magnetic gap into what life would actually feel.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honesty over hype: nothing is trained, so nothing can leak. Weights were set before seeing results. Our weakest case (flat plains, AUC 0.53) is shown, not hidden. Scores rank places against each other and are not "percent Mars". Mars targets use real rover landing coordinates. Every brief lists its limits.
